## What session 11 is for {.scrollable}
::::: columns

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The mathematics

- Set up a **difference-in-differences** design and identify the four cells
- Read the **interaction coefficient** as the estimate
- State the **parallel-trends** assumption and how you would probe it
- Explain why **two-way fixed effects** can mislead under staggered adoption (the **forbidden comparison**)
- Say what difference-in-differences **cannot** fix, and what to report

::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The Python

- Print the adoption table and plot each cohort before estimating anything
- Build the four cells, then get the same number from an interaction in `smf.ols`, clustered by unit
- Estimate an event study by regression and let the pre-period speak for the design
- Handle staggered adoption with `diff_diff.CallawaySantAnna`, open up TWFE with `BaconDecomposition`, and test sturdiness with `HonestDiD`
- Write up the estimate with its objective, its evidence and its breakdown value

::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The international business

- Evaluate a policy that arrived in different countries at different times
- Defend parallel trends as an argument, not as a test that passed
- Say plainly what the design cannot rescue

# Before the session {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

::: {style="margin-top: 1.0em; color:#F7F4ED"}
### What would have happened otherwise?
:::

## What to do, and how long it takes

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Read the paper, looking for its difference-in-differences | 45–60 min |
| **2** | Get the paper's data, check the course data, and map your project | 15 min |
| **3** | Attempt the self-check | 15 min |

::: {.warn}
The lecture assumes all three are done. The practice assumes the data is already cached on your
machine.
:::

## 1 · Read the paper

**Cavallo, Gopinath, Neiman & Tang (2021), *Tariff Passthrough at the Border and at the Store: Evidence from US Trade Policy*, American Economic Review: Insights 3(1)**

::: {.muted}
[Read the article](https://doi.org/10.1257/aeri.20190536)
:::

::: {.step}
**Objective.** Find the **difference-in-differences inside the paper**, so that in the practice you can
reproduce its number and know which choices the authors had to defend.
:::

Read for the **argument**, not for coverage. Annotate the answers to five questions; the practice opens
with them:

| | Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | What is **treated**, and what is the **control** group? | the second difference is only as good as the controls |
| **2** | What are the **dates**: before, after, and is adoption staggered? | decides which comparisons exist |
| **3** | Which **coefficient** is the estimate, and in what **units**? | the number you will reproduce |
| **4** | What evidence do they show for **parallel trends**? | an event study, a pre-period, an argument? |
| **5** | What could **change at the same time** as the treatment? | the first objection a referee would raise |

::: {.muted}
Not every answer is stated in the paper. A question the paper leaves open is a finding: write it down.
:::

## 2 · Get the paper's data

::: {.step}
**Objective.** Have the paper's replication package on your machine, so that the first twenty minutes
of the practice are spent reproducing a number, not downloading one.
:::

**a) The paper's replication package** — Harvard Dataverse

::: {.step}
[10.7910/DVN/JV7FCH](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/JV7FCH)
:::

This deposit sits behind a Dataverse **guestbook**, so it cannot be fetched with `curl`:

1. open the DOI above in a browser;
2. click **Access Dataset → Download ZIP**, and accept the terms once;
3. unzip it into `11-causal-inference-did/data/replication/`, from the repository root.

::: {.warn}
`data/replication/` is git-ignored, so nothing large is committed. Keep the authors' own
structure — do not tidy it.
:::

## 2b · The course data, and your project

::: {.step}
**Objective.** Check that the data and the estimators of the practice run on your machine, and decide
which four columns of **your** project a difference-in-differences would use.
:::

```python
import qmib
import diff_diff as dd

ai = qmib.load("angle_c_country")           # the practice ground: AI strategies, 30 countries
print(ai.shape, ai["has_ai_strategy"].sum(), "country-years with a strategy")
print("diff-diff", dd.__version__)          # the estimators of the lecture and the practice
```

::: {.check}
**You should see** `(330, 33) 61 country-years with a strategy` and a version of `diff-diff` of 3.11
or later. It downloads once and caches as parquet, so the practice works whatever the room's wifi is
doing. `ModuleNotFoundError: diff_diff`: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, environment active.
:::

**Then, on paper, map your project** ([`RESEARCH-MANDATES.md`](../../RESEARCH-MANDATES.md)) onto the four
columns every estimator asks for:

| Column | On the course data | On your project |
|---|---|---|
| **unit** | `geo`, the country | ? |
| **time** | `time`, the year | ? |
| **outcome** | `ai_use_any`, % of firms using AI | ? |
| **adoption year**, 0 if never | from `has_ai_strategy` | ? which policy, which date, for which units? |

::: {.warn}
If no unit is ever treated, none stays untreated, or none is observed **before** its treatment, the
design cannot apply to your project. Knowing that before class is a full answer, and it is what step 3 of
the practice will ask.
:::

## 3 · Self-check, and what the session will ask of you

Answer these on paper. If you cannot, that is what the lecture is for.

::: {.tight}
1. **Compute one.** Full-time staff per fast-food restaurant: New Jersey went from 20.44 to 21.03 after its
   minimum wage rose; Pennsylvania, which did not change its wage, from 23.33 to 21.17. What is the
   difference-in-differences, and what would New Jersey have reached without the rise?
2. **Name the differences.** Which of the two subtractions removes what is **constant** about the treated
   group, and which removes what happened to **everyone**?
3. **The assumption.** Parallel trends is about which years: before the policy, or after? Why can no test
   prove it?
4. **Session 10 against session 11.** Matching needed every confounder measured. What does
   difference-in-differences need instead?
5. **The paper.** Which claim rests on the difference-in-differences, and how hard does it lean on it?
:::

By the end of the session you should be able to:

::: {.tight}
- Set up a **difference-in-differences** design and identify the four cells
- Read the **interaction coefficient** as the estimate
- State the **parallel-trends** assumption and how you would probe it
- Explain why **two-way fixed effects** can mislead under staggered adoption
- Say what difference-in-differences cannot rescue
:::

::: {.get}
**Arrive with:** the paper annotated against the five questions · the replication package unzipped ·
the check in 2b run once · your project mapped onto four columns · your self-check answers on paper.
:::

## Before you run anything

Everything runs in the **VS Codium terminal**, from the repository root, with the project
environment active. Activate it in **every new terminal**, not only the first:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate        # macOS and Linux
```

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\activate           # Windows (PowerShell)
```

::: {.check}
Your prompt must begin with **`(.venv)`**. Without it `python` and `pip` are your system's, and
nothing the course installed is visible to them.
:::

::: {.muted}
`ModuleNotFoundError` means the packages went somewhere else, or were never installed. Check the
prompt first, then `pip install -r requirements.txt` — **from the repository root, with the
environment active**. Building the environment from scratch is Session 01, step 1.4.
:::
